title: Between Two Rounds
logline: At a small elders' home, the same two carers move within one hour from helping a resident through a hard, frightened moment to sitting with another whose grandchild has just visited with good news.
human_question: Can the same person really be fully present for someone's pain and someone else's joy within the same hour?

situation.what_happens: Two carers work a shift in a small residential home for old people. The day is mostly routine: washing, feeding, medication, moving people, waiting. Inside it, the demands change completely from room to room. One resident is frightened or in pain and needs someone to stay. Another has had a visitor and wants to talk about it. A third wants nothing and is left alone. The carers move between these without any transition and without naming what they are doing.
situation.who_is_involved: Two carers on the same shift, probably underpaid and certainly under-staffed; residents with varying capacity to consent; families who visit, and families who do not; whoever runs the home.
situation.what_is_at_stake: For the residents, dignity and the right not to be looked at. For the carers, being judged on the hardest hour of their week. For the viewer, whether care is a mood a person has or a response they keep making.
situation.how_it_unfolds: A shift has a fixed frame and unpredictable contents. Its pressures are staffing, illness, deaths, family conflict, and the emotional cost of doing this for years. It ends with a handover and begins again. Reality decides what any single day contains, whether the good news arrives while anyone is there, and whether the carers will describe the switching for themselves.

concept_merge.why_together: C030's ledger of which factors can join which minds carries the specific rule this film rests on: the occasional beautiful factors arrive one at a time, so compassion and gladness cannot fill the same moment. C095 gives the four shapes one care can take and names the failure of each, including the even-mindedness that remains when nothing more can be done. C024 adds that these two are the boundless factors, which are supposed to reach whoever is in front of you rather than the residents a carer happens to like. Together they describe the actual texture of care work as a rapid alternation rather than a temperament.
concept_merge.what_it_reveals: That what looks like one continuous quality in a good carer is, in this account, a fast sequence of different responses, and that its discipline is impartiality rather than intensity.

concept_links.why: Compassion and sympathetic joy each need a specific person actually in view, and the occasional beautiful factors arise one at a time [C030-P:L25; C030-P:L39]. An honest note from the digest: the narrow point the film rests on, that compassion and gladness never share a moment, is supported in both sources [C027-M:L7], while the wider rule that only one of the five occasional beautiful factors arises at a time comes from one source and is flagged for expert check.

The four abidings include equanimity, described as what remains when there is nothing more to be done, and its failure is ignorant indifference, so stepping back is not the same as ceasing to care [C095-P4:L39; C095-P4:L60].

Compassion and sympathetic joy are the two boundless factors, arising only when a suffering or a happy being is in view and meant to extend without favourites [C024-P:L81; C024-P:L91]. Here, among people who are not the carers' own kin, the source's demand for impartiality applies straightforwardly.

what_the_viewer_could_understand: Care is not one fixed mood: compassion arises toward someone who is suffering and gladness toward someone who is happy, each answering the person actually in front of you, so the same carer moves between them within an hour.
what_must_be_real: Residents' own informed, ongoing consent, or their families' and guardians' where capacity is limited, with the right to withdraw at any time. No frailty shown for effect, no moment of distress filmed that the person has not agreed to, and no scheduling of care around the film.
position_hint: closing candidate: it turns the group's warmth toward bodies that are failing, which is where the next stage begins.
risks: High: residents' dignity and their capacity to consent
Institutional and family permission may be withdrawn at any point
Implying that anybody's age, illness or dependence is explained by what they did earlier in life
drop_if: The home or its residents cannot give informed, ongoing consent
Filming would change how care is given

connections.note: Both are closing candidates handing the group on to the body's fragility, one among the sick and one among the old.
Both ask how one person's care changes shape for different people within the same day, one among kin and one among strangers.

selection.reason: Used by its episode and the group's clearest carrier of the ledger of factors in ordinary good minds.

unknowns: No participant or event has been found or confirmed. Everything here is a research direction.
evidence_class_note: Editorial proposal. No location, scene or shot decisions are made at the idea stage.
